questions.q: $1g$ of a liquid is converted to vapour at $3 \times {10}^{5}Pa$ pressure. If $10 %$ of the heat supplied is used for increasing the volume by $1600{cm}^{3}$& during this phase change, then the increase in internal energy in the process will be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
As pressure against which expansion is happening is constant, work done can be written as& $= P\Delta V$

$= \left(3 \times {10}^{5}\right) \times\left($1600 $\times {10}^{- 6}\right)

$= 480J$
As only $10 %$ of heat is used in work done.

The rest goes in increase in internal energy, which is $90 %$ of heat.
Change in internal energy $= 0 . 9 $\times$4800 = 4320J$

$

questions.q: A balloon filled with helium&  \left(32 ° Cand1 .7 atm\right)$& bursts. Immediately after wards the expansion of helium can be considered as :& $
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
A thermodynamic process that happens without transmitting heat or mass between the thermodynamic system and its surroundings is known as an adiabatic process.

An irreversible process is one in which the system and its surroundings are unable to revert to their original states.

Bursting of a balloon is an irreversible adiabatic process, because energy can not be restored in this process.

questions.q: A sample of an ideal gas is taken through the cyclic process $ABCA$ as shown in figure. It absorbs, $40J$ of heat during the part $AB$, no heat during $BC$ and rejects $60J$ of heat during $CA$. A work of $50J$ is done on the gas during the part $BC$. The internal energy of the gas at $A$ is $1560J$. The work done by the gas during the part $CA$ is
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
& In the part $A \to B$, the volume remains constant. Thus, the work done by the gas is zero. It is given that the heat absorbed by the gas is $40J$. From first~law of thermodynamics, $Q = \Delta U + W$

$⇒ 40 = \Delta U + 0 ⇒ \Delta U = 40J$

or $\Delta U = {U}_{B} - {U}_{A} = 40J$

The increase in internal energy from $A$ to $B$ is $40J$. The internal energy is $1560J$ at $A$, then

${U}_{B} - 1560 = 40J ⇒ {U}_{B} = 1600J$

In the part $B \to C$, the work done by the gas is $W = 50J$ and no heat is given to the system. Again using~$Q = \Delta U + W$

$0 = \Delta U - 50$~or~$\Delta U = {U}_{C} - {U}_{B} = 50J$

${U}_{C} - 1600 = 50J ⇒ {U}_{C} = 1650J$

~The change in internal energy from $C \to A$,

$∆ U = 1560 - 1650 = - 90J$

The heat given to the system is $Q = - 60J$

Using $Q = \Delta U + W$, we get~$W = Q - ∆ U = - 60 - \left(- 90\right) = 30J$

questions.q:
Match the thermodynamics processes taking place in a system with the correct conditions. In the table : $∆ Q$is the heat supplied, $∆ W$ is the work done and $∆ U$ is change in internal energy of the system.

~ Process ~ Condition
(I) Adiabatic (A) $∆ W = 0$
(II) Isothermal (B) $∆ Q = 0$
(III) Isochoric (C) $∆ U e 0, ∆ W e 0, ∆ Q e 0$
(IV)

Isobaric

 (D) $∆ U = 0$
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
In Adiabatic& $\Delta Q = 0, i . e . ,$~Exchange of heat does not take place.

In Isothermal~$\Delta U = 0, i . e . ,$~Temperature does not change therefore internal energy also remains constant.

In Isochoric~$\Delta W = 0, i . e . ,$~Volume remains constant therefore work done is zero.

In Isobaric~$∆ U e 0, ∆ W e 0, ∆ Q e 0$
$W = P . ∆ V$, Volume changes so work done is not equal to zero.
$∆ U = \dfrac{f}{2}P ∆ V$, Volume changes therefore internal energy changes.
~$∆ Q = n{C}_{p} ∆ T$, Temperature changes therefore heat also changes.

questions.q:
Given below are two statements:

Statement I: If heat is added to a system, its temperature must increase.

Statement II: If positive work is done by a system in a thermodynamic process, its volume must increase.

In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below
options: Statement I is true but Statement II is false
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
If heat energy is added to a thermodynamic system, one part increases the internal energy and the other part performs some work.

If heat is added to a system, the system can do work without changing its internal energy.& Hence, statement 1 is false.

The formula to calculate the work done is given by

$W = ∫ PdV$

From the above equation, it can be concluded that if~$W > 0$, i.e., work is done by the system, its volume must increase. Hence, statement II is true.

questions.q: A thermodynamic system is taken from an original state $A$ to an intermediate state $B$ by a linear process as shown in the figure. Its volume is then reduced to the original value from $B$ to $C$ by an isobaric process. The total work done by the gas from $A$ to $B$ and $B$ to $C$ would be :
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
Work done during the path $A \to B$ can be written as $\begin{cases}{W}_{AB} & = & \dfrac{1}{2} ( 8000 + 4000 ) dyne{cm}^{- 2} \times \dfrac{1N}{{10}^{5}dyne} \times \dfrac{1{cm}^{2}}{{10}^{- 4}m^{2}} \times \left(7 - 3\right)m^{3} \\ & = & 2400J\end{cases}$

The work done during the process $B \to C$ is given by

$\begin{cases}{W}_{BC} & = & \left(4000dyne{cm}^{- 2} \times \dfrac{1N}{{10}^{5}dyne} \times \dfrac{1{cm}^{2}}{{10}^{- 4}m^{2}}\right) \times \left(3 - 7\right)m^{3} \\ & = & - 1600J\end{cases}$

Hence, the total work done is given by

$\begin{cases}W & = & {W}_{AB} + {W}_{BC} \\ & = & 2400J - 1600J \\ & = & 800J\end{cases}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
The amount of work done for the given process should be zero, as the process is an isochoric process.

Thus, the change in internal energy will be equal to the heat exchanged in the process. Mathematically,

$Q = ∆ U$

Now,

$∆ U = ms ∆ T . . . \left(1\right)$

From equation (1), it follows that

$\begin{cases}∆ U & = & 0 . 08 \times (170 \times4 . 18 ) \times5J \\ & \approx& 284J\end{cases}$

questions.q: At a certain temperature, the degrees of freedom per molecule for gas is $8$. The gas performs $150J$ of work when it expands under constant pressure. The amount of heat absorbed by the gas will be _____~$J$.
questions.subject: Physics
questions.solution:
For constant pressure process,

Work done is given by& $W = nR\Delta T = 150J$, here,~$R$~is gas constant.

Now, for above process,~$f = 8$.

So, specific heat at constant pressure is~${C}_{P} = \left(1 + \dfrac{f}{2}\right)R$.

Amount of heat adsorbed by the gas is~

$Q = n{C}_{P}R\Delta T = \left(\dfrac{f}{2} + 1\right)nR\Delta T = \left(\dfrac{8}{2} + 1\right)150 = 750J$
